name: Ferry Building
blurb: The 1898 terminal and its 245-foot clock tower, modelled on Seville's Giralda. Ferries still leave from the piers behind it; the hall inside is a food market.

cam.label: StreamTime cam on the Embarcadero by Pier 23, a few piers up from the Ferry Building

name: Salesforce Tower
blurb: San Francisco's tallest building at 1,070 feet (2018). The LED crown on top plays a video art piece at night.

name: Transamerica Pyramid
blurb: William Pereira's 853-foot pyramid (1972), the city's tallest for 46 years and still its most recognisable skyline shape.

name: Salesforce Park
blurb: A 5.4-acre park on the roof of the Salesforce Transit Center, with a gondola up from Mission Street.

name: Millennium Tower
blurb: The 58-storey condo tower famous for sinking and tilting, now being shored up with piles to bedrock.

name: Embarcadero Center
blurb: Four slab towers and a hotel joined by sky bridges, John Portman's 1970s city within the city.

name: Hyatt Regency
blurb: Portman's stepped hotel with a 17-storey atrium, the lobby in Mel Brooks' High Anxiety.

name: Embarcadero Plaza
blurb: The plaza and park at the foot of Market Street, home of the Vaillancourt Fountain and the winter ice rink.

name: Bay Bridge
blurb: The 1936 western span to Yerba Buena Island. At night its cables carry 25,000 LEDs in The Bay Lights.

name: Pier 7
blurb: A long public fishing pier with old-fashioned lamps and a straight-on view of the Bay Bridge.

name: 555 California
blurb: The dark granite former Bank of America headquarters (1969), where Dirty Harry's rooftop scenes were shot.

name: Palace Hotel
blurb: Rebuilt in 1909 after the earthquake, with the glass-roofed Garden Court dining room.

name: Rincon Park
blurb: Waterfront lawn under Cupid's Span, the giant bow and arrow by Oldenburg and van Bruggen.

name: Portsmouth Square
blurb: Chinatown's living room, and the spot where the city began as Yerba Buena in 1835.

name: Oracle Park
blurb: The Giants' ballpark (2000) on the edge of McCovey Cove, where home runs splash into the bay and kayakers wait for them.

name: Chase Center
blurb: The Warriors' arena in Mission Bay, opened in 2019 when the team moved back across the bridge from Oakland.

name: SFMOMA
blurb: Mario Botta's striped-oculus museum (1995) with Snøhetta's rippled white extension stacked behind it (2016).

name: Yerba Buena Gardens
blurb: A lawn and waterfall on the roof of Moscone Center, with the Martin Luther King Jr. memorial behind the falls.

name: South Park
blurb: An oval of grass from the 1850s, modelled on a London square, later the hangout of the first dot-com boom.

name: 4th & King Caltrain
blurb: The San Francisco end of Caltrain, where electric trains leave for San Jose.

name: One Rincon Hill
blurb: The 60-storey tower beside the Bay Bridge approach, with a 50-ton water tank at the top that damps it in the wind.

name: Mission Dolores
blurb: Mission San Francisco de Asís. Its small adobe chapel, finished in 1791, is the oldest intact building in the city; the 1918 basilica stands beside it.

name: Mission Dolores Park
blurb: A sloping lawn with a view across the Mission to downtown. The land was two Jewish cemeteries until the city bought it in 1905.

name: Castro Theatre
blurb: Timothy Pflueger's 1922 movie palace, with its neon blade sign over Castro Street.

name: Duboce Park
blurb: A small neighbourhood park and dog lawn. N Judah trains come out of the Sunset Tunnel at its western end.

name: 24th Street, Noe Valley
blurb: Noe Valley's main street of shops and cafés, in a valley that Twin Peaks shelters from much of the fog.

name: San Francisco Armory
blurb: A castle-like National Guard armory built in 1914 at 14th and Mission.

name: The Women's Building
blurb: Its walls carry MaestraPeace, a 1994 mural painted by seven women artists.

name: Coit Tower
blurb: The 210-foot Art Deco column on Telegraph Hill (1933), paid for by Lillie Hitchcock Coit's bequest to beautify the city. Murals from 1934 line the lobby.

name: Lombard Street
blurb: The crooked block between Hyde and Leavenworth: eight hairpin turns laid in 1922 because the hill was too steep to drive straight down.

name: Pier 39
blurb: A shopping pier opened in 1978. The sea lions arrived on its marina docks after the 1989 earthquake and never left.

name: Washington Square
blurb: North Beach's front lawn, under the twin spires of Saints Peter and Paul Church.

name: Twin Peaks
blurb: Two 922-foot summits near the middle of the city, with the widest view of it, when the fog allows.

name: Sutro Tower
blurb: The 977-foot three-legged TV and radio mast on Mount Sutro (1973), often wading in fog.

cam.label: ALERTCalifornia / UC San Diego, Sutro Tower 2

name: Glen Canyon Park
blurb: A wild canyon with Islais Creek running through it, rock outcrops and eucalyptus, a few minutes' walk from Glen Park BART.

name: Palace of Fine Arts
blurb: Bernard Maybeck's rotunda and lagoon from the 1915 Panama-Pacific Exposition, the one building of the fair kept, rebuilt in concrete in the 1960s.

name: Fort Mason
blurb: An old Army post whose piers shipped troops to the Pacific in World War II. The pier sheds are now theaters, galleries and event halls.

name: Marina Green
blurb: A long lawn on the bay for kites, picnics and joggers, with the Golden Gate Bridge off to the west.

name: Ghirardelli Square
blurb: The old Ghirardelli chocolate factory, turned into shops and restaurants in the 1960s, its sign lit up over the bay.

name: Aquatic Park
blurb: A sheltered cove inside a curving pier, where swimmers train in the cold bay all year.

name: Lafayette Park
blurb: A hilltop park in Pacific Heights, ringed by mansions, with views over the bay.

name: Alta Plaza Park
blurb: A terraced hilltop park in Pacific Heights, looking north over the Marina to the Golden Gate.

name: Presidio Main Post
blurb: The parade lawn of the old Presidio, ringed by brick barracks. A military post from 1776 to 1994, now a national park.

name: Bernal Heights Park
blurb: A bare, grassy hilltop about 430 feet up, with views across the whole city. Mostly dogs and their people.

name: Precita Park
blurb: A long, narrow park at the foot of Bernal Hill, where the Mission meets Bernal Heights.

name: Mountain Lake
blurb: One of the city's few natural lakes, at the Presidio's southern edge. Juan Bautista de Anza's expedition camped here in 1776.

name: Presidio Golf Course
blurb: Laid out in 1895 for the Army post's officers, one of the oldest golf courses in the West, now public.

name: Crissy Field
blurb: An Army airfield from 1921, restored in 2001 as a beach, tidal marsh and lawn along the bay, looking out to the Golden Gate Bridge.

name: USS Pampanito
blurb: A World War II submarine that made six war patrols in the Pacific, now a museum ship tied up at Pier 45. You can climb down through the torpedo rooms.

name: Yoda Fountain
blurb: Yoda stands on a fountain outside Lucasfilm's offices at the Letterman Digital Arts Center in the Presidio. The lobby is open to visitors on weekdays.

name: Pier 39 sea lions
blurb: California sea lions hauled out on the K-Dock floats. They showed up after the 1989 earthquake, liked the herring, and stayed; hundreds in winter, fewer in summer.
